name: TPS5430DDAR
title: 3 A, 500 kHz step-down converter with integrated high-side switch, 5.5 V to 36 V input
summary: The TPS5430 and TPS5431 are fixed 500 kHz voltage-mode buck converters with a 110 mΩ high-side N-channel MOSFET on chip, needing an external catch diode, inductor and output capacitor. They deliver 3 A continuous (4 A peak) at outputs adjustable down to 1.221 V. The TPS5430 runs from 5.5 V to 36 V and the TPS5431 from 5.5 V to 23 V. Compensation is internal; protection covers cycle-by-cycle and hiccup current limit, output overvoltage and thermal shutdown, and ENA shuts the part down to 18 µA.

notes: Misprint: the TPS5430DDA operating temperature 0 to 0 should read -40 to 125, as for every other part number.
Qualified variants of the TPS5430 exist: TPS5430-Q1 (automotive) and TPS5430-EP (enhanced product).

circuits.title: 12 V input to 5.0 V output
circuits.description: A 3 A buck converter making 5 V from a 10.8 V to 19.8 V input. C1 decouples VIN. C2 between BOOT and PH carries the high-side gate drive. When the internal switch is off, D1 carries the inductor current from ground into L1. L1 and C3 filter the switched PH node into the 5 V output. R1 and R2 divide the output down to the 1.221 V reference at VSNS. EN drives the ENA pin. GND and the PowerPAD go to ground.

parts.note: input decoupling; ceramic X5R or X7R, rated 25 V, ripple current capacity above 3 A
Sumida CDRH104R-150: saturation current 3.4 A, RMS current 3.6 A
Diodes Inc.; 40 V reverse, 3 A forward, 0.5 V forward drop
Sanyo POSCAP 10TPB220M: 10 V, ESR 40 mΩ max, ripple current 3 A

notes: U1 pins 2 and 3 are both NC and are left open.

circuits.title: 10 V – 35 V input to 5 V output
circuits.description: The same buck stage run from a 10 V to 35 V input, over the TPS5430's wide input range, with a larger 22 µH inductor and a lower loop crossover. Two 4.7 µF capacitors in parallel decouple VIN. TP6 is a test point on the switch node.
notes: U1 pins 2 and 3 are both NC and are left open.

circuits.title: 9 V – 21 V input to 5 V output
circuits.description: A TPS5431 buck converter making 5 V from a 9 V to 21 V input. It uses an 18 µH inductor, larger than in the 12 V design, and crosses over at a lower loop frequency. C3 is a Sanyo POSCAP 10TP220M.
notes: U1 pins 2 and 3 are both NC and are left open.

circuits.title: Ceramic output filter capacitors, 10 V – 24 V to 3.3 V
circuits.description: A 3.3 V, 3 A buck converter from 10 V to 24 V using only ceramic filter capacitors. With a ceramic output capacitor the loop needs an external network around the divider, giving two poles and two zeros: C6 sits across R1, and the series pair R3 and C7 sits across R2. C4 from VSNS to ground improves load regulation. R1 and R2 set 3.3 V. D1 is an MRBS340 Schottky.

parts.note: kept below one tenth of C6

notes: U1 pins 2 and 3 are both NC and are left open.

operation.text: Fixed-frequency voltage-mode PWM buck with an integrated 110 mΩ high-side N-channel MOSFET and an external catch diode. The error amplifier compares VSENSE with the 1.221 V reference through an on-chip type III compensation network; the PWM comparator sets the duty cycle by comparing that error voltage with a ramp. Input voltage feed-forward scales the ramp amplitude with VIN so the modulator gain stays at about 25, which improves regulation against input changes and the response to input steps.
The switching frequency is fixed internally at 500 kHz and cannot be adjusted.
A bandgap-based reference, trimmed in production to 1.221 V at room temperature. It is also the lowest output voltage the part can regulate to.

ENA is active high with an internal current source pulling it up (5 µA in the block diagram), so the regulator runs with ENA open. Below 0.5 V the part stops switching, the slow start resets and the supply current falls to 18 µA typical; above 1.3 V (maximum start threshold) it starts. Where ENA is driven, an open-drain or open-collector output drives it. At start-up the reference rises linearly from zero to 1.221 V in the slow-start time, 8 ms typical.

Below the UVLO start threshold (5.3 V typical) the part is held off and the slow start is grounded. Once VIN crosses the threshold the slow start is released and the converter starts; it then runs until VIN falls below the stop threshold, 330 mV lower typical. Operation is recommended above 5.5 V, though the part can run down to the UVLO voltage.
A 0.01 µF ceramic capacitor, low ESR, X5R or X7R, from BOOT to PH supplies the high-side gate drive. The bootstrap recharge diode is internal.

The switch current is sensed as the drain-to-source voltage of the high-side MOSFET. After a leading-edge blanking time, a voltage above the overcurrent threshold ends that switching cycle early (cycle-by-cycle limit, 5 A typical). Under a hard overload such as a short circuit the part goes into hiccup mode: the reference is grounded and the switch stays off for the hiccup time (16 ms typical), then the converter restarts through slow start.
A comparator holds the high-side switch off while VSENSE is above 112.5 % of VREF and releases it when VSENSE falls back below that level, limiting overshoot when the output recovers from a fault.
Above the trip point (162 °C typical) the reference is grounded and the switch turned off. The part restarts through slow start once the junction has cooled 14 °C below the trip point.

An input decoupling capacitor is required, 10 µF ceramic X5R or X7R recommended; a smaller value may serve if the input ripple voltage and current ratings are respected. Its voltage rating must exceed the highest input voltage plus ripple. Bulk capacitance may be needed if the converter is more than about 2 inches from the source; a 100 µF electrolytic is a typical choice.

Because compensation is internal, only a limited range of output filter values is supported. Inductors are typically 10 µH to 100 µH, rated for the RMS and saturation currents. Keep the closed-loop crossover between 3 kHz and 30 kHz, where the internal compensation gives enough phase boost, and below the output capacitor's ESR zero. For phase margin, the zero formed by the capacitor's lowest ESR should sit not much higher than the 24 kHz and 54 kHz poles of the internal compensation. The output capacitor's voltage rating must exceed the output voltage plus half the ripple, with derating. A 0.1 µF ceramic bypass may be added at the output.

An external diode from PH to GND is required. Its reverse rating must exceed the highest PH voltage, VIN(MAX) + 0.5 V; its peak current rating must exceed IOUT(MAX) plus half the inductor's ripple current. A low forward drop raises efficiency, since the diode conducts for longer than the switch is on; check its power dissipation.

With ceramic output capacitors the loop needs an external compensation network around the feedback divider (R3, C4, C6, C7 in the ceramic circuit), and the LC resonance should be no higher than 7 kHz. Ceramic capacitance falls with applied voltage; a low output voltage such as 3.3 V reduces the effect.

Place a ceramic bypass capacitor of low ESR (4.7 µF minimum, X5R or X7R) as close to VIN as possible and keep the loop through VIN, the capacitor and GND small, by carrying the top-layer ground from beneath the IC out beside the VIN trace. Put a top-layer ground area under the IC with an opening for the PowerPAD, stitched by vias to inner ground planes, with extra vias at the ground ends of the input and output capacitors; tie GND to that area. PH is the switching node: place the inductor very close to PH with minimum copper area to limit capacitive coupling, keep the catch diode close to reduce the output current loop, and keep the boot capacitor close with short traces. Keep the loop from PH through the inductor, output capacitor and GND small. Route the feedback divider trace away from PH, under the output capacitor or on another layer; with the grounding pattern of the layout example, ENA is reached through a via to another layer. The PowerPAD must be soldered to the board for thermal performance, and GND must connect to it.
